changes.year1_quote: An investment in our common stock involves risks and uncertainties and investors should consider carefully the following risk factors before investing in our securities.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: An investment in our common stock involves risks and uncertainties and investors should consider carefully the following risk factors before investing in our securities.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2021 disclosure addresses the same general investment risks and uncertainties, with no material change to the underlying economic risk. The language is substantively identical, so it is retained.
changes.title: General Risk Factor Disclosure

changes.year1_quote: Demand for advertising is highly dependent upon the strength of the U.S. economy, both in the markets our stations serve and in the nation as a whole. During an economic downturn, demand for advertising often decreases.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Demand for advertising is highly correlated with the strength of the U.S. economy, both in the markets our stations serve and in the nation as a whole.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 disclosure continues to identify the same underlying economic risk: advertising demand and revenues depend on U.S. economic conditions and may be adversely affected by a decline. The wording changes from “highly dependent” and explicitly describing downturn-driven decreases to “highly correlated,” but the economic risk is not materially weakened or removed.
changes.title: Advertising Demand And Economic Conditions

changes.year1_quote: For example, increasing demand for content generated for consumption through other forms of media such as Amazon Prime, Disney+, HBO Go, Hulu, or Netflix, could cause our advertising revenues to decline as a result of changes to the ratings of our programming, which may materially negatively affect our business and results of operations.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: For example, increasing demand for content generated for consumption through other forms of media such as Amazon Prime Video, Disney+, HBO Max, Hulu, Netflix, or Peacock could cause our advertising revenues to decline as a result of changes to the ratings of our programming, which may materially negatively affect our business and results of operations.
changes.reasoning: The underlying economic risk is unchanged: alternative media and evolving consumption habits may reduce television audiences and ratings, making stations less attractive to advertisers and reducing advertising revenue. The revisions mainly update service names (for example, HBO Go to HBO Max and adding Peacock) without changing the risk or its severity.
changes.title: Competition From Alternative Media

changes.year1_quote: A resurgence in the rate of COVID-19 infections that is significant enough to force widespread business closures could materially and adversely affect our financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: A resurgence in the rate of COVID-19 infections that is significant enough to force widespread business closures could materially and adversely affect our financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.
changes.reasoning: The core economic risk—COVID-19 infection resurgences potentially causing widespread business closures and materially harming financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows—is stated verbatim in Year-2. The additional discussion updates pandemic developments but does not weaken or remove the underlying risk.
changes.title: COVID-19 Pandemic Business Impact

changes.year1_quote: The failure of our information technology systems to perform as we anticipate could disrupt our business and could result in transaction errors, processing inefficiencies, broadcasting disruptions, and loss of sales and customers, causing our business and results to be impacted.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: The failure of our information technology systems to perform as we anticipate could disrupt our business and could result in transaction errors, processing inefficiencies, broadcasting disruptions, and loss of sales and customers, causing our business and results to be impacted.
changes.reasoning: The underlying economic risk—operational and financial harm from inadequate or failed information technology systems—is unchanged. Year-2 adds that some systems are hosted and operated by third-party vendors, but this supplements rather than changes the disclosed risk.
changes.title: Information Technology System Failures

changes.year1_quote: These measures, however, may not be sufficient in preventing or timely detecting breaches or cyber-attacks due to the evolving nature and ever-increasing abilities of cyber-attacks.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: While the measures we employ meet or exceed industry standards they nonetheless may not be sufficient in preventing or timely detecting breaches or cyber-attacks due to the evolving nature and ever-increasing abilities of cyber-attackers.
changes.reasoning: The core economic risk—cyberattacks or breaches may evade prevention or timely detection despite the company’s protective measures—remains materially disclosed in Candidate 1. Year-2021 also retains the consequential risks, insurance limitation, and adds vendor-related cyber disruption; the added detail does not weaken or remove the Year-2020 risk.
changes.title: Cybersecurity Incidents And Protection

changes.year1_quote: As has historically been the case in the broadcast sector, loss of, or changes in, affiliation agreements or retransmission consent agreements could adversely affect operating results for our stations
changes.year2_quote_or_null: As has historically been the case in the broadcast sector, loss of, or changes in, affiliation agreements or retransmission consent agreements could adversely affect operating results for our stations
changes.reasoning: The Year-2021 candidates retain the same underlying economic risks: loss or unfavorable changes in affiliation agreements, non-renewal or termination and replacement-programming costs/revenue impacts, and alternative distribution platforms diluting network-programming value. The only changes are immaterial wording, updated expiration dates, and platform names.
changes.title: Network Affiliation Agreement Risks

changes.year1_quote: On occasion, we may not be able to agree on mutually acceptable terms when negotiating such agreements. When this happens, the MVPD may be required to cease airing our programming (commonly referred to as a “blackout” or “going dark”).
changes.year2_quote_or_null: On occasion, we may not be able to agree on mutually acceptable terms when negotiating such renewals as we experienced in renewal negotiations with a major broadcast satellite provider in early October 2021. When this happens, the MVPD will be required to cease airing our programming (commonly referred to as a “blackout” or “going dark”), and we will not be compensated by the MVPD during the period of the blackout as was the case with the broadcast satellite provider.
changes.reasoning: The core economic risk is retained: failure to reach retransmission-consent terms can cause MVPD blackouts, loss of related compensation, and adverse business results. Year-2 updates the wording and adds a concrete example, but does not materially weaken or remove the risk.
changes.title: Retransmission Consent Agreement Risks

changes.year1_quote: Broadcast companies operate in a highly competitive environment and compete for audiences, advertising and marketing services revenue and quality programming.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Broadcast companies operate in a highly competitive environment and compete for audiences, advertising and marketing services revenue and quality programming.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 candidate reproduces the same underlying economic risk: intense broadcast competition affecting audience share, advertising and marketing services revenue, programming costs, and business results. The disclosure is substantively unchanged.
changes.title: Broadcast Industry Competition

changes.year1_quote: In addition, the FCC and Congress are contemplating several new laws and changes to existing media ownership and other broadcast-related regulations, regarding a wide range of matters (including the number of stations a company may own within a single market or nationwide).
changes.year2_quote_or_null: In addition, the FCC and Congress may enact new laws and regulations, and/or changes to existing laws and regulations, that could impact media ownership and other broadcast-related activities.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2021 disclosure retains the same underlying economic risks: changing media/broadcast regulation may create uncertainty, affect affiliation or retransmission leverage and revenues, increase costs, reduce station valuations, and jeopardize license renewal. The language is generalized and rephrased, but the economic substance and risk severity are not materially changed.
changes.title: Media Ownership And Licensing Regulation

changes.year1_quote: Our stations are subject to various obligations and restrictions under the Communications Act of 1934 as amended (the “Communications Act”), and FCC regulations. These requirements may be affected by legislation, FCC actions, or court decisions, and any such changes may affect the performance of our business, such as by imposing new obligations or by limiting our television stations’ exclusivity or retransmission consent rights.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Our stations are subject to various obligations and restrictions under the Communications Act of 1934, as amended (the Communications Act), and FCC regulations. These requirements may be affected by legislation, FCC actions, or court decisions, and any such changes may affect the performance of our business, such as by imposing new obligations or by limiting our television stations’ exclusivity or retransmission consent rights.
changes.reasoning: The core regulatory risk is retained: changes in legislation, FCC action, or court decisions could impose obligations, limit exclusivity or retransmission consent rights, and affect the business. Candidate 1 also retains the related risk that more restrictive ownership rules could impair acquisition-led growth, while Candidate 2 retains the DOJ antitrust and divestiture risk; the changes are primarily factual updates and stylistic wording.
changes.title: Regulatory Environment And Growth

changes.year1_quote: If the spin-off was determined to be taxable for U.S. federal income tax purposes, TEGNA and its stockholders that are subject to U.S. federal income tax could incur significant U.S. federal income tax liabilities.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: If the spin-off was determined to be taxable for U.S. federal income tax purposes, TEGNA and its stockholders that are subject to U.S. federal income tax could incur significant U.S. federal income tax liabilities.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 disclosure retains the same economic risk: the Cars.com spin-off could be treated as taxable, creating significant U.S. federal income tax liabilities for TEGNA and certain stockholders. The update to the IRS examination and statute-of-limitations timing does not alter the underlying risk disclosure.
changes.title: Cars.com Spin-Off Tax Liability

The economic risk is therefore absent rather than reworded or absorbed.
changes.title: Activist Shareholder Actions and Disruption

changes.year1_quote: Strategic acquisitions, investments and partnerships could pose various risks, increase our leverage and may significantly impact our ability to expand our overall profitability.
changes.reasoning: No Year-2021 disclosure meaningfully addresses the economic risks associated with strategic acquisitions, investments, or partnerships, including leverage, integration, control, partner financial difficulties, regulatory approvals, or realization of expected benefits. changes.title: Strategic Acquisitions, Investments and Partnerships

changes.year1_quote: Volatility in the U.S. credit markets could significantly impact our ability to obtain new financing to fund our operations and strategic initiatives or to refinance our existing debt at reasonable rates and terms as it matures
changes.year2_quote_or_null: If our operating results deteriorate significantly, we may not be able to pay amounts when due and a portion of these maturities may need to be refinanced. Access to the capital markets for longer-term financing is generally unpredictable and volatile credit markets could make it harder for us to obtain debt financings.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2021 disclosure retains the same underlying economic risks: volatile credit markets may impair access to financing and make refinancing maturing debt more difficult. Changes in debt amounts, maturities, and the addition of Merger Agreement restrictions do not materially alter the retained credit-market and refinancing risk.
changes.title: Credit Market Volatility and Refinancing Risk

changes.year1_quote: Goodwill and other intangible assets were approximately $5.47 billion as of December 31, 2020, representing approximately 80% of our total assets.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Goodwill and other intangible assets were approximately $5.42 billion as of December 31, 2021, representing approximately 78% of our total assets.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2021 disclosure retains the same underlying economic risk: goodwill and intangible assets may require impairment charges due to adverse operating, market, or valuation conditions. The numerical updates and minor wording change do not alter the substance of the risk.
changes.title: Intangible Asset Impairment Risk

changes.year1_quote: We had $355 million in floating interest rate obligations outstanding on December 31, 2020, and therefore are subject to changes in the amount of interest expense we might incur. A 50 basis point increase or decrease in the average interest rate for these obligations would result in an increase or decrease in annual interest expense of $1.8 million.

The lower outstanding balance and corresponding lower estimated impact change the magnitude of exposure, not the presence or nature of the risk.
changes.title: Market Risk and Interest Rate Exposure
